rv.q: Mischievous makeover of Jerome K Jerome’s perennial classic from adapter Al Smith

Al Smith’s dramatisation neatly juggles chronology (the sixth chapter is his first scene) and anchors the book’s best set pieces (swan attack, putrid cheese, a murder investigation) in a new narrative where the blokes are heading to Oxford for Harris’s wedding, his choice of best man a bugbear.
What they've created this time is fun and lively, but it struggles to find its feet.
